provenance_note: Honey blocks are generated by the organ itself; cases vary only HOW MUCH of the block is overwritten. There is no real ransomware sample in this corpus and none was executed.
positive_definition: Any write to a honey block at all. This organ is a tripwire, not a classifier: the blocks are files no legitimate process should ever touch.
negative_definition: Reads, writes to neighbouring real files, and writes to non-honey paths.

cases.label: attack
cases.rationale: The encryption pass the trap exists for: every byte of the honey block rewritten, which is the first 4 KB any ransomware touches.

cases.label: attack
cases.rationale: A writer that stops after the header still touched the trap.

cases.label: attack
cases.rationale: The weakest possible touch. Included because the organ claims FIRST-write detection.

cases.label: benign
cases.generator: read the honey file, write nothing
cases.rationale: A scanner reading files must not trip a write trap.

cases.label: benign
cases.generator: write to a real file in the same directory
cases.rationale: An application writing a real file in the same directory as the traps. The FS hook fires on every write in the directory, so a trap that keys on the directory rather than on its registered blocks would raise here — and would then be unusable on any shared folder.

cases.label: benign
cases.generator: write to a path the organ never armed
cases.rationale: The hook fires on every write; only registered hives matter.
